subject: VM evidence rotation and CVE ownership — clarification for SOC2 auditor
messages:
From: Peter Jones <peter.jones@acme-payments.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Security <security@acme-payments.com>, Auditor QA <audits@finserve.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Oct 2025 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC2 request — VM scan cadence, SLA exceptions, and remediation evidence

David —

Quick one from our SOC2 auditor (copied). They want a compact packet that shows: the cadence of vulnerability scans covering our hosted endpoints, an index of CVEs identified in the last 12 months with ownership and closure timestamps, and any SLA exceptions (hotpatches/extended windows) tied to justification. Auditor asked for delivery within 48 hours if possible.

Can Redwood provide:
- Scan index (CSV) with find IDs, severity, first-found/last-seen dates, owner/team;
- A short attestation listing remediation commitments for P1/P2/P3 and actual close dates for any CVEs in the last quarter;
- Any documented exceptions to standard SLA (why, duration, mitigation).

We can forward this to our auditor once we have a single zip/drive link. Appreciate a single point of contact for the packet — is that you?

Thanks,
Peter
Peter Jones
Head of Security Operations, Acme Payments

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Peter Jones <peter.jones@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Oct 2025 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC2 request — VM scan cadence, SLA exceptions, and remediation evidence

Pete —

Thanks for the note and for looping in the auditor. Yes — happy to be the point of contact. We'll assemble a compact evidence packet and share a Drive link. Plan below: 

1) Scan index CSV (covering 12 months) — includes vulnerability ID, CVE, severity, first-found, most-recent-seen, owner (team/person), remediation status
2) Remediation attestation PDF — statements for P1/P2/P3 SLAs (45/90/180 day baseline), plus a table of CVEs closed in the last quarter with timestamps and references to patch artifacts
3) SLA exception log — short notes for any cases where our standard SLAs were extended, with compensating controls and rollback plan references

Kimberly — can you attach the attestation PDF and the patch-rollforward CSV? Marissa — can you confirm whether we should include a canned cover letter for the auditor (short statement + contact)?

We will aim to have the Drive link to you by end of day (24 hours). If the auditor needs DocuSign-stamped attestation, we can route that after initial delivery (link below).

-David
David Kim
Security Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Peter Jones <peter.jones@acme-payments.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Oct 2025 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC2 request — VM scan cadence, SLA exceptions, and remediation evidence

On Thu, Oct 9, 2025 at 9:05 AM David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Kimberly — can you attach the attestation PDF and the patch-rollforward CSV?

David / Pete — attaching the requested artifacts. Notes below and in the attestation PDF (remediation-attestation-acme-202510.pdf).

Summary points (high level):
- Scan cadence: automated authenticated network + agent-based OS scans run weekly for prod clusters, with incremental daily vulnerability probes for critical endpoints. Full coverage matrix in the CSV.
- SLA cadence (our baseline commitments): P1 (critical; exploit in wild): 45 days to remediation or mitigant; P2 (high): 90 days; P3 (medium/low): 180 days. These are described in the attestation.
- Exceptions in scope: 3 exceptions in the last 12 months — two short extensions (one due to vendor patch delay, one scheduled rollback window) and one hotpatch response that required a 72-hour emergency window. Each exception has a compensating control entry and a linked patch artifact (see patch-rollforward-202509.csv).
- Ownership: column "owner" in the scan index maps to our internal on-call (team alias) and the ticket URL for traceability. Where an external vendor owned the fix, that is called out in the owner_notes column.

Attachments (stubs):
- remediation-attestation-acme-202510.pdf (signed attestation; includes signed timestamps and a summary table of CVEs closed Q3 2025)
- acme-scan-index-202509.csv (scan index export with 12-month window)
- patch-rollforward-202509.csv (patch artifacts & rollback notes)

If the auditor would like the attestation notarized via DocuSign, we can generate that this morning and send a DocuSign link. 

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head, Vulnerability Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Peter Jones <peter.jones@acme-payments.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Auditor QA <audits@finserve.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Oct 2025 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC2 request — VM scan cadence, SLA exceptions, and remediation evidence

David / Kimberly —

Received — thank you. The packet looks to cover what the auditor asked for. A couple of quick clarifications they requested: 
- In the attestation PDF, can you add the phrase "scan cadence applies to production-facing infrastructure and customer data paths" (they want explicit scope language)?
- For the three exceptions, the auditor wants a one-line rationale per exception in the exception table (we can include that in the cover letter).

If you can add those two small edits and re-upload to the Drive link, we'll forward to the auditor today. Also please go ahead and generate the DocuSign attestation (fine if a follow-up link is used) — Auditor prefers a signed attestation on file.

I'll stand by for the edited PDF/Drive link. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Best,
Peter
Head of Security Operations, Acme Payments
